title: Kernel-aware admission controller for prefill/decode with probabilistic acceptance and rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an admission controller layer that scores candidate model+kernel routes for prefill and decode phases. The controller emits a probabilistic acceptance score rather than a binary pass/fail to enable soft-commit speculative decoding, with deterministic fallback rules and an operator runbook for rollbacks. Goal: reduce cost and latency by routing more requests to faster low-cost kernels/models while preserving quality through measurable acceptance telemetry and quick rollback on regressions.
background: Current runtime routing makes mostly binary routing decisions and relies on fixed thresholds and heuristic probes. We've observed opportunities where kernel-level characteristics (e.g., KV-cache locality, fusion-friendly kernels, quantization artifacts) could be used to prioritize routes but require a softer acceptance mechanism to avoid increased false-accepts that degrade output quality. Prior tickets explored prefills, probes, and speculative handoffs but lacked a lightweight admission scoring layer for gradual rollout and observability.
proposed_design: 1) Admission API: runtime will call /admit with request fingerprint (model_family, model_variant, kernel_fingerprint, prefill_length_estimate, latency_budget, cost_budget). Controller returns {acceptance_score: float(0..1), confidence_bucket: string, recommended_fallbacks: [model_variant]}.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller responds within 200ms p95 for admission queries under normal load. 2) Acceptance_score correlates with observed decode-level quality: acceptance->no statistically-significant drop in BLEU/ROUGE/chrF or LM-based quality metric on monitored prompt set (+/-1% tolerance). 3) Telemetry exposes acceptance_rate, acceptance_precision (fraction of accepts that met quality baseline), rollback_triggers fired. 4) Canary rollout reduces median cost per token for targeted route by >=8% without increasing customer-facing error rate.
telemetry_and_metrics: Instrument admission decisions with these tags: kernel_fingerprint, model_variant, acceptance_score, prefill_len_bin, latency_budget_bin, route_outcome (accept, fallback, rollback), fallback_reason. Track metrics: admission_qps, admission_latency_p50/p95, acceptance_rate, acceptance_precision, quality_regression_rate, avg_token_cost_delta, fallback_rate, rollback_count. Add alert rules: acceptance_precision < 0.95 for 5m -> page on-call; rollback_count > 5 in 15m -> auto-disable canary.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): enable admission in shadow for 2 weeks on 5% of traffic; record decisions, do not act. Phase 1 (canary soft-commit): enable probabilistic acceptance for 0.5% -> 5% traffic with automatic soft-commit where accepts are applied but requests carry a fallback ticket allowing decode to switch mid-stream. Observe metrics for 1 week. Phase 2 (ramped): 5% -> 25% then 25% -> 100% if acceptance_precision and quality metrics hold. Each phase includes kill-switch and automated rollback if quality_regression_rate or acceptance_precision breach thresholds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation and API contract. Integration tests for runtime->admission roundtrip under mocked kernel fingerprints. Regression tests using stored prompt set to measure quality delta under accepted routes. Load test the admission API at peak QPS simulated (target 3x expected prod). Chaos tests: force admission API timeouts and verify graceful fallback to default route within latency SLOs.
notes: Controller must be lightweight and horizontally scalable; prefer local cache of recent kernel_fingerprint scores to avoid critical path network hops. Consider embedding a small LRU-scored table in the serving runtime as a fast-path and fallback to controller only on cold fingerprints.
